claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has native surface and processing-derived grain-boundary and dislocation distributions.
Controlled thermal pre-oxidation can form a uniform, adherent oxide film on Q235 steel.
An adherent pre-formed oxide film can suppress corrosion-related degradation of Q235 steel in aggressive humid environments.
Heating Q235 steel in air at 300 °C for 1 hour will promote formation of a homogeneous, adherent iron-oxide layer.
The density, uniformity, adhesion, and phase constitution of the oxide film govern its protective quality.
The pre-formed oxide film limits transport of oxygen, moisture, and ions to the steel substrate.
The oxide film reduces the number of active sites available for localized corrosion.
Localized corrosion can initiate at grain boundaries or surface defect sites in Q235 steel.
Restricted corrosive-species transport and fewer active sites delay corrosion initiation and progression.
Pre-oxidized specimens will exhibit lower corrosion-related weight loss than untreated specimens under identical exposure conditions.
Pre-oxidized specimens will exhibit less pitting than untreated specimens.
Pre-oxidized specimens will exhibit higher electrochemical impedance than untreated specimens.
The proposed controlled comparison uses 90% relative humidity at 25 °C and 75 °C for 168 hours, with assessments every 24 hours.
Failure of pre-oxidized samples to show statistically significant improvement in weight loss, pitting density, or EIS response relative to controls would falsify the hypothesis.
